macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures edge higher ahead of inflation data
items.summary: U.S. stock futures were slightly higher as investors assessed whether technology shares could recover from the recent AI-driven selloff. The S&P 500 rose 0.31% and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.09% in the latest session, while investors awaited consumer- and producer-price data and technology earnings.

items.title: Strong jobs report lifts expectations for December Fed rate hike
items.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double economists’ expectations, while unemployment fell to 4.1%. Markets priced in roughly an 80% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase in December, increasing pressure on risk assets ahead of the CPI release.

items.title: Asian stocks steady as AI and geopolitical concerns ease
items.summary: Asian equities were broadly stable as concerns about the technology selloff and Middle East tensions receded. The dollar remained firm as traders increased bets on a December Federal Reserve rate hike.

items.title: AI trade remains under pressure ahead of CPI and tech earnings
items.summary: Investors continued to reassess the sustainability and cost of the artificial-intelligence infrastructure boom after a sharp technology-led market decline. CoreWeave, Applied Materials and Cisco Systems are among the companies scheduled to report, while Tuesday’s CPI is the week’s main macroeconomic catalyst.

items.title: Nvidia board opens investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation into CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang’s reported relationship with a businesswoman described by U.S. intelligence agencies as a Chinese spy. The development pressured Nvidia futures and added uncertainty to the broader AI trade.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum fall as crypto market liquidations top $1 billion
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $75,039, down about 1% over 24 hours, while Ethereum fell roughly 4.3% to $2,141.45. Network-wide liquidations reached approximately $1.016 billion, including $915 million in long positions.[2][8]

items.title: FinCEN action against MEXC triggers withdrawal concerns
items.summary: After FinCEN issued special measures against MEXC Global, users reported delayed or restricted transfers to other exchanges, including OKX, Binance, and Gate. The order had not officially taken effect, and the scope of the restrictions remained unclear.[2]

items.title: Binance to close some European customer accounts
items.summary: Binance is preparing to close affected accounts in France, Spain, Italy, and Poland by December 31 after the EU’s MiCA transition period expires. Remaining balances may incur a monthly fee beginning November 29.[6]

items.title: EU launches task force targeting crypto-based sanctions evasion
items.summary: The European Union established a 12-month task force to coordinate enforcement against digital-asset networks allegedly facilitating evasion of sanctions on Russia.[6]

items.title: Binance hack-linked funds reportedly converted into Bitcoin
items.summary: Elliptic co-founder Tom Robinson said approximately $175 million in stolen altcoins were converted into about 2,300 Bitcoin through transfers spanning 16 blockchains, more than 20,000 wallets, and at least 65,000 transactions.[2]

items.title: Keplr users warned of possible private-key exposure
items.summary: Keplr Wallet said a vulnerability in Web3Auth infrastructure may have exposed private keys belonging to some users who logged in through Google or Apple.[2]

items.title: Circle receives OCC bank charter as crypto infrastructure expands
items.summary: Circle reportedly received a U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency bank charter, while SWIFT went live with 17 banks in a development highlighting continued integration between traditional financial infrastructure and digital assets.[1]

items.title: US spot Bitcoin ETF holdings exceed 2.06 million BTC
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds reportedly held more than 2.06 million Bitcoin, equivalent to approximately 10.24% of the cryptocurrency’s supply.[7]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic AI development pace reportedly doubles
items.summary: A METR analysis found Anthropic’s AI-assisted research and development progressed roughly twice as quickly as a year earlier, raising new questions about accelerating capability growth and safety oversight.

items.title: LG opens free access to K-Exaone 2.5
items.summary: LG AI Research announced free API access to K-Exaone 2.5 after reporting more than 70% performance improvement over eight weeks. The model is positioned for agentic AI applications and is described as competitive with leading open-weight systems based on LG’s evaluations.

items.title: NIH awards $3.4 million for AI delirium detection research
items.summary: Northwell Health’s Feinstein Institutes received a $3.4 million NIH grant to develop AI tools for detecting and preventing hospital delirium, a condition associated with elevated risks to older adults’ brain health.

items.title: Japan announces AI-focused emergency cybersecurity package
items.summary: Japan unveiled a 10 billion yen cybersecurity package that includes AI and cyber-response teams, aiming to improve information sharing and speed assistance as AI-generated threats and cyberattacks increase.

items.title: Faraday Future announces OmniMind embodied-AI model
items.summary: Faraday Future and FF Robotics said their OmniMind model ranked first on the RoboColiseum embodied-AI leaderboard as of November 6, ahead of several prominent robotics and frontier-model systems. The company is also pursuing partnerships with U.S. security and inspection-robotics integrators.

items.title: Preferred Networks releases finance-focused PLaMo 3.0 Fin
items.summary: Preferred Networks released PLaMo 3.0 Fin, an 8-billion-parameter finance-oriented language model, under a community license, adding to the expansion of specialized open or openly available models.

items.title: OpenAI names MegazoneCloud a Select Partner
items.summary: MegazoneCloud was named a Select-tier partner in the OpenAI Partner Network, reflecting continued expansion of enterprise AI distribution and implementation partnerships.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA VI launch preparations dominate gaming news
items.summary: Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to launch on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S after two delays. The game is expected to become one of the industry’s biggest releases, with reports also highlighting a physical edition that may contain a download code rather than a disc.[1][5]

items.title: 007 First Light offered as a free trial
items.summary: IO Interactive’s 007 First Light is available to try free on PlayStation 5, Xbox and PC through a promotional initiative. The action-stealth game launched in May 2026 and has received generally positive player reactions.[7]

items.title: Zero Ops: Covert Warfare enters PS5 and PC closed beta
items.summary: A four-person development team has begun a closed beta for Zero Ops: Covert Warfare, a tactical shooter inspired by SOCOM. The Unreal Engine 5 game is planned for PC and PS5.[4]

items.title: Macronix to exit Nintendo cartridge-chip business
items.summary: Macronix, a major supplier of ROM chips used in Nintendo game cartridges, is phasing out that business to focus on AI hardware. Nintendo can reportedly use other suppliers for physical game cards.[6]

items.title: Skydance reportedly cuts jobs in gaming divisions
items.summary: Skydance has reportedly laid off an unspecified number of employees in its video-game divisions following Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. The available report did not provide details on the number of affected workers or projects.[9]

items.title: Xbox Game Pass announces anniversary-week additions
items.summary: More than 10 titles are scheduled for Xbox Game Pass during Xbox’s 25th-anniversary week, including Football Manager 27, Warhammer Survivors and Tanuki: Pon’s Summer. John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando is also listed for November 12.[8]
